claim_one_line: THE INSTRUMENT ALREADY EXISTED, AND THIS ARC'S FIRST DRAFT WAS WRONG ABOUT THE COST. Banked NEGATIVE: this arc set out to build an arbitrary-precision Maass solver because B1006 named MORE DIGITS as the value layer's bottleneck; it built one that DOES NOT WORK, claimed a cost overturn that is FALSE, and then found that a working one has been on main since B922. (1) THE HEADLINE IS A CORRECTION OF THIS ARC'S OWN FIRST DRAFT: a working, sealed, arb-based 25-digit solver is ALREADY IN THE REPOSITORY at frontier/B878_maass_upper_window/branch_cell9_rung1_v2.py, whose docstring reads 'conformant to sealed prereg v3 (169e9042)' -- THE SAME SEAL HASH B922 NAMES -- so it is the script behind the 58.1-hour run, and it was on main before this arc started. This seat wrote a new solver WITHOUT READING IT: the NINTH INSTANCE this session of grepping claims instead of reading code, B1006's cell D having duplicated B922 the same way five hours earlier. (2) THE COST CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN AND B798 STANDS IN FULL, INCLUDING ITS COST ESTIMATE. The first draft claimed B798's cost estimate was priced against arithmetic that is not what arb does. That is FALSE and B798's own text refutes it in the very sentence that makes the estimate: '4-5 orders of magnitude beyond the certified run, ON A DIFFERENT NUMERICAL STACK (arb/mpmath Bessel, mp linear algebra)'. B798 NAMED ARB, priced an arb instrument, and included arb's overhead as a factor of 10-100. And the 58.1-hour run DID use flint/arb: flint.ctx.prec = int((DIGITS+45)*3.33)+250, K_ir(r,x) = flint.acb(x).bessel_k(i*r), an flint.acb_mat LU solve, at n ~ 1300. WHERE THE ERROR WAS, PRECISELY: B798's cost model has TWO terms and this seat used only one -- modes scale ~LINEARLY WITH PRECISION (900 modes to 11250 at 100 digits) and the dense solve is CUBIC in modes (1953x at 100 digits), while this arc HELD THE MODE COUNT FIXED at 300-1000 and varied only dps. The per-operation timings measured here (1000 K_ir in 0.07/0.10/0.15 s and a 200x200 acb_mat solve in 0.34/0.48/0.64 s at 25/50/100 dps, i.e. arb overhead under 2x) are CORRECT AS MEASUREMENTS and DO NOT SUPPORT THE CONCLUSION DRAWN FROM THEM: precision is cheap PER OPERATION, but the cost is that higher precision DEMANDS MORE MODES and the solve is cubic in modes, so varying dps at fixed M measures the one term that was never the problem. NOTHING IN THIS ARC OVERTURNS B798's LAW OR ITS COST ESTIMATE. (3) THE SOLVER FAILED ITS OWN GATE (recover B922's r = 4.9000853730625213014795758 or claim nothing): M=40 gives g ~ 1e26, M=80 is smooth with no sign change. FIVE DIFFERENCES from the working solver, FOUR OF THEM FIXED IN ITS SOURCE WITH THE REASON IN A COMMENT: (a) NO COLUMN EQUILIBRATION -- the working code divides each column by |Y*K(2pi|mu|Y)| and states why, that the truncation-edge dynamic range (~1e-32 at the real run) collapses to O(1) 'which arb's certified LU requires at n >~ 1300', so THE 1e26 IS EXACTLY THIS AND THE FIX WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN (B792's float64 scanner does the same, svd(V / cn[None,:]), and says so in its docstring); (b) NO RISEN-POINT FILTER -- the working code keeps a point only if mv and ts > Y*(1+1e-20), because a point that does not move gives f(z,Y) = f(z,Y), AN IDENTICALLY ZERO ROW, and this seat filtered nothing so the system was singular by construction; (c) MODES CHOSEN BY COUNT, NOT RADIUS -- the working code takes all mu with |mu| <= R_cut = (pi*r/2 + margin)/(2*pi*Y), the truncation set by where K_ir dies, whereas 'the first M by |mu|' is not the same set and has no convergence argument behind it; (d) Y = 0.28 against the sealed Y = 0.75; and (e) THE WRONG INDICATOR FOR THE JOB, the conceptual error -- the held-out-row residual g(r) is what the working code uses but ONLY for LOCAL REFINEMENT INSIDE AN ALREADY-BRACKETED ROOT (a damped bracketed secant), while DETECTION is done by SIGMA_MIN OF THE COLUMN-NORMALIZED V(r) in the float64 scanner, which DIPS at an eigenvalue; this seat used a REFINEMENT indicator to SEARCH, which is why scanning found no sign change -- g(r) IS NOT BUILT TO HAVE ONE. (4) WHAT SURVIVES: the exact Z[omega] geometry port (91 moves, tau = 2 sqrt3 i to +-4.8e-40, exact dual lattice, working pullback) is CORRECT AND REDUNDANT, since branch_cell9_rung1_v2.py already has _mpgen/_mpmoves/mp_reduce doing the same job in mpmath and already drives arb from it; and ONE genuinely new observation kept because it is not in the working source, that since 1/(2 sqrt3) is about 0.289, ordering Lam* by |mu| gives ONLY m in {-1,0,1} EVEN AT M=30 -- a consequence of choosing modes by count, and another reason not to. HONEST STANDING: THE PROGRAMME CAN REPRODUCE lambda_2 AND HAS BEEN ABLE TO SINCE B922, WITH THE CODE ON MAIN. What this arc contributes is a corrected cost picture (B798 WAS RIGHT), a precise diff against the working instrument for whoever touches it next, and one more datum on the failure mode that has now cost this session nine arcs: READ THE CODE BEFORE REBUILDING IT. No number produced by arb_maass.py enters any ledger, and the file is kept only as the record of the failed attempt. SCOPE: an INSTRUMENT arc asserting no new mathematics about the object; no SM quantity involved, Gate 5 untouched; it changes NO claim's standing and REMOVES a claim this seat made earlier today.
